title: Linear Pair Theorem
summary: Two adjacent angles form a linear pair when their non-common sides are opposite rays. The two angles add to 180°, so they are supplementary.
proofIdea: Use the Protractor Axiom to assign coordinates 0° and 180° to the opposite rays of the straight line. If the shared ray has coordinate t°, then ∠AOB = t° and ∠BOC = (180 - t)°, whose degree values add to 180°.
explorationPrompt: Move the shared ray and compare the two adjacent angles with their 180° total.

proofSteps.title: Set the straight-angle coordinates
proofSteps.detail: Assign coordinate 0° to ray OA and 180° to its opposite ray OC.

proofSteps.title: Read the two angle sizes
proofSteps.detail: If ray OB has coordinate t°, then ∠AOB = t° and ∠BOC = (180 - t)°.

proofSteps.title: Add the adjacent angles
proofSteps.detail: The sum t + (180 - t) simplifies to 180, so the linear pair is supplementary.

corollaries.title: Corollary: several angles on a straight line
corollaries.statement: If several adjacent angles partition a straight angle, then they add to 180°. The intermediate coordinate differences cancel when added.
corollaries.proof: Assign the ordered rays coordinates 0 = b₀ < b₁ < ⋯ < bₙ < bₙ₊₁ = 180. By the Protractor Axiom, each adjacent angle has size (bᵢ − bᵢ₋₁)°. Adding these differences cancels every intermediate coordinate, leaving only 180 − 0.

corollaries.title: Corollary: a congruent linear pair
corollaries.statement: If two angles in a linear pair are congruent, each is a right angle. Consequently, the line containing their common side is perpendicular to the line containing their non-common sides.
corollaries.proof: Let each congruent angle have size x°. By the Linear Pair Theorem, x + x = 180°, so 2x = 180° and x = 90°. Each angle is therefore a right angle, and the line through O and B is perpendicular to the line through A, O, and C by definition.
